taxonomic_note: Legacy Master Plant Pool name Chamaesyce nutans is normalized to the current accepted Euphorbia name.
look_here_first: FIRST LOOK AT LEAF SIZE AND SHAPE. Nodding spurge (Euphorbia nutans) is usually an ASCENDING or arching annual with relatively LONG opposite oblong leaves (8–40 mm), strongly UNEQUAL leaf bases, and finely TOOTHED margins. Its small cyathia have white-to-pink gland appendages; nearby mature fruit is a smooth, THREE-LOBED capsule. Several photographed dark seeds show low IRREGULAR wrinkles, not the high parallel cross-ridges of E. prostrata. Against E. villifera, nutans usually has bigger leaves and small fringed or divided scale-shaped stipules (FNA; full stipule pattern not directly proved by existing photos), whereas villifera tends toward smaller ovate leaves and minute separate threadlike stipules. Don't decide from a red leaf blotch, hairiness, or smooth fruit alone. Hays native-by-county badge remains unaudited.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum: opposite leaves, milky latex, tiny cyathia, and a 3-lobed capsule. In E. nutans, plant stature and leaf architecture are unusually helpful before moving to fruit and seed.
morphology_keys.growth_form: Annual with taproot; stems usually ascending, occasionally erect, often arching or nodding near branch tips, roughly 20–80 cm.
morphology_keys.stems: Sparsely to moderately pilose/villous or with short incurved hairs, commonly concentrated at nodes and distal portions; hairs may form two bands on opposite sides of the stem.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite; blades oblong to oblong-lanceolate, about 8–40 × 3–12 mm. Base strongly asymmetric: one side angled/rounded, the other truncate to cordate-auriculate. Margins serrulate; upper surface often has a reddish blotch or mottling but can lack it.
morphology_keys.stipules: Small scales, usually distinct, sometimes basally connate on one side of stem; irregularly toothed, fringed, or divided.
morphology_keys.cyathium: Cyathia solitary at distal nodes or in small terminal cymose clusters. Four green to reddish-purple glands with white or pinkish ovate-to-broadly-elliptic appendages.
morphology_keys.seed: Seeds dark brown, elliptic-ovoid to ovoid, rounded-angular in cross section, about 1–1.6 × 0.5–0.8 mm; surface finely and irregularly wrinkled or with faint shallow transverse ridges.
best_field_traits: ascending to erect annual with arching branch tips
red central leaf blotch often present but not required
nutans stipules are irregularly toothed/fringed/divided small scales 1–1.5 mm; contrast with villifera filiform stipules 0.3–0.7 mm, but present node photo does not resolve complete pattern
Against villifera: nutans 8–40 mm leaf blade versus villifera mostly 3–12 mm (overlap possible); confirm margin/fruit/node not one character
Deep seed sculpture is low irregular wrinkles, NOT the conspicuous cross-bars of prostrata; existing seed photograph has uncalibrated background grid
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Teach opposite leaves and their STRONGLY unequal bases first, then fine edge teeth, then hairless fruit and microscopic seed wrinkles. Unlike E. villifera, E. nutans generally has larger leaves and fringed/divided 1–1.5 mm scalelike stipules, not minute separate filiform stipules. Both can have ascending branches and hairless capsules; leaf spot or hairiness alone is not diagnostic. E. maculata grows as a low mat and has fine hairs on capsule faces; E. prostrata has fruit-keel hairs and strong transverse seed ridges.

photo_note: Four individually cleared public-eligible diagnostic photographs (Kenraiz CC BY-SA, HermannSchachner CC0, Douglas Goldman CC BY-SA and Dale Lee Denham-Logsdon CC BY-NC for noncommercial use). comparisons.key_distinctions: E. nutans rises well above the ground and carries much larger leaves. The combination of ascending/arching stems, strongly asymmetric serrulate leaves, and glabrous capsules separates it from the low sandmats.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: BIG OPPOSITE TOOTHED LEAVES — SMOOTH CAPSULE — WRINKLED SEED
steps: Find opposite 8–40 mm leaves with strongly asymmetrical bases; look for fine marginal teeth rather than relying on a red leaf spot.
Look at several arching/ascending stems rather than confusing the pictured upper shoot with the whole habit; the existing public gallery has no full rooted growth-form shot.
In the flowering tips locate small cyathial gland appendages, then identify the smooth slightly three-lobed fruit nearby; the structures are NOT petals and flowers in the ordinary sense.
Look at a node under a lens for fringed/divided scales, distinct or basally joined on one side. Existing closeup marks the LOCATION but not complete stipule identity, fusion, or size.
Compare the photographed true dark seeds' low irregular wrinkles with the sharply cross-ridged seed of E. prostrata. The background grid on our source seed photo is not calibrated.
Against E. villifera, check longer often oblong nutans leaves versus smaller ovate villifera leaves; microscopic stipule shape is the stronger tie-break when leaves overlap.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Use only verified arrows in gallery. Flowering-tip source is not a whole plant, and node source does not prove scale-like stipule fusion. The seed image may be reused only while the site remains genuinely noncommercial. Hays nativity review intentionally paused.
